newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Six die, nine disappear in Colombian massacre.
newsitem.headline: Six die, nine disappear in Colombian massacre.

text.p: Six people, including an eight-year-old boy, were massacred by a suspected right-wing paramilitary gang in Colombia's northern Cesar province on Sunday, national radio reported.

Nine other people disappeared, presumed kidnapped, and one was hospitalized with multiple bullet wounds after a group of about 60 men, dressed in camouflage clothing, raided the village of Media Luna, close to Colombia's border with Venezuela, according to the RCN radio network.

The attack took place just before midday (1500 GMT) in the remote village, about 25 miles (40 km) north of provincial capital Valledupar. Police told RCN that the motives for the attack were not yet clear.

The attackers arrived in three pick-up trucks and cut telephone lines before opening fire on their victims. Before leaving, the gang scrawled pictures of machine-guns on walls in the village together with the initials "ACCU", which stands for the so-called Peasant Self-Defence Group of Cordoba and Uraba -- a shadowy paramilitary group, possibly backed by regular members of the armed forces and police.

The Peasant Self-Defence Group of Uraba and Cordoba has unleashed a bloody war against the country's leftist guerrillas, especially in northern and northwest Colombia where the rival groups battle for control of lucrative contraband routes.
Since the summer, the paramilitary group has kidnapped a number of close relatives of rebel chieftains in what they claim is a bid to stifle guerrilla activities.
Police were not immediately available to confirm details of the massacre.
